topic_tag: a truce between two river towns
prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
blank_sentence: Writing a century later, one historian called the truce between the towns from 1790 to 1815 ______.

worlds.passage: For most of the eighteenth century, two towns on opposite banks of a salmon river tore down each other's fish weirs whenever the run was good. By 1790 most families on each bank had a married son or daughter on the other, and the magistrates' books for 1790 to 1815 record almost no cut weirs. Each town's boats kept to their own half of the river, and each council fined any of its own men caught on the far bank. In those years neither council passed a single resolution concerning the other town. Writing a century later, one historian called the truce between the towns from 1790 to 1815 ______.
worlds.explanation: Both towns held back and each policed its own men, while neither council passed any resolution concerning the other town; combining the restraint with that silence shows the peace was never spoken or written, so the truce was "tacit." "Tactical" fails because the peace rested on lasting family ties, not on a short-term aim. "Token" fails because cut weirs almost disappeared. "Unilateral" fails because both councils restrained their own men.

tactical.quote: had a married son or daughter on the other
tactical.why: the restraint rests on kinship, a lasting tie, not on a calculated move toward a passing goal

token.why: the truce changed behavior, so it was not a truce in name only

unilateral.quote: each council fined any of its own men
unilateral.why: both towns held back, so the restraint was not one-sided

worlds.passage: For most of the eighteenth century, two towns on opposite banks of a salmon river tore down each other's fish weirs whenever the run was good. In 1790 a canal company petitioned to buy the fishing rights of both banks, and the two councils, writing to each other for the first time in a generation, agreed to fight the petition together. While the case dragged on, the magistrates' books record almost no cut weirs. The company withdrew its petition in 1815, and within a season each town was cutting the other's weirs again. Writing a century later, one historian called the truce between the towns from 1790 to 1815 ______.
worlds.explanation: The peace began when a common threat appeared and ended as soon as that threat was withdrawn; combining the start and the end shows it served a short-term purpose, so the truce was "tactical." "Tacit" fails because the councils wrote to each other and agreed. "Token" fails because weir-cutting almost stopped while the case ran. "Unilateral" fails because both towns acted together.

tacit.quote: writing to each other for the first time
tacit.why: the councils' agreement was put in writing, not left unspoken

token.why: the peace held in practice for as long as the case lasted, so it was not in name only

unilateral.quote: agreed to fight the petition together
unilateral.why: both towns joined in, so the arrangement was not one-sided

worlds.passage: For most of the eighteenth century, two towns on opposite banks of a salmon river tore down each other's fish weirs whenever the run was good. In 1790 the two councils signed a truce at a feast on the bridge, and they renewed it with the same toasts every spring until 1815. In no year of the twenty-five, the magistrates' books show, were fewer weirs cut on either bank than in the decades before. Neither council fined a single man for crossing to the far bank, and the feast grew larger every year. Writing a century later, one historian called the truce between the towns from 1790 to 1815 ______.
worlds.explanation: The truce was signed and toasted every year, while weir-cutting never fell below its old rate in any year and no one was punished; combining these shows the truce existed in name only, so it was "token." "Tacit" fails because the truce was signed openly. "Tactical" fails because a truce made for an aim still holds while the aim lasts, and this one never held in any year. "Unilateral" fails because neither town held back.

tacit.quote: signed a truce at a feast
tacit.why: the truce was openly made and celebrated, not unspoken

tactical.quote: In no year of the twenty-five
tactical.why: a truce serving a short-term purpose changes behavior while that purpose lasts; this one never changed behavior at all

unilateral.quote: fewer weirs cut on either bank
unilateral.why: neither side held back, so there was no one-sided restraint

worlds.passage: For most of the eighteenth century, two towns on opposite banks of a salmon river tore down each other's fish weirs whenever the run was good. In 1790, after two of its boys drowned in a fight on the river, the upstream council declared that its men would cut no more weirs and fined every man who did. The magistrates' books record no weirs cut by upstream men from then until 1815. The downstream council never answered the declaration, and its men went on cutting upstream weirs in most years. Writing a century later, one historian called the truce between the towns from 1790 to 1815 ______.
worlds.explanation: Only the upstream town held back, and the downstream town neither agreed nor stopped, so the truce was "unilateral." "Tacit" fails because the upstream town announced its restraint openly. "Tactical" fails because the restraint followed a drowning and served no aim of advantage. "Token" fails because the upstream town really did stop cutting weirs.

tacit.why: the restraint was announced, not unspoken

tactical.quote: after two of its boys drowned
tactical.why: the passage gives grief, not any short-term advantage, as the reason for the restraint

token.quote: record no weirs cut by upstream men
token.why: the upstream town kept its word, so the truce was not in name only
